v.why: Large batches give few updates in 243 epochs, so raising LR rescues step-limited undertraining more than at small batches.
At aggressive LR, larger batches denoise gradients and reduce step count, damping divergence instead of starving training.
With one hidden layer, width is the only capacity route, so widening helps more than in deeper nets.
More units sum more Adam-sized updates into each pre-activation, so wide nets destabilize faster at high LR.
Narrow layers bottleneck capacity, so an extra layer adds needed expressivity that wide nets already have.
Update errors compound through three layers, so raising LR destabilizes deep nets more than shallow ones.
Wide nets have excess capacity that overfits small tabular sets, so more L2 helps them more than narrow nets.
L2 on every layer multiplicatively shrinks the deeper signal path, so raising alpha underfits deep nets more.
sklearn divides the L2 gradient by the minibatch size, so tiny batches amplify an alpha increase into underfitting.
Under strong L2, extra units spread the penalized signal across more weights and recover underfit capacity.
